reasoning: The deepseek model completed a full review of all files and correctly identified this as a standard binary AUR package. The PKGBUILD downloads a prebuilt binary from the project's own GitHub releases with pinned SHA256 checksums. The prepare() function clones the project's own repository to fetch documentation/examples - while this uses an unpinned ref (default branch), it's from the project's own upstream and doesn't execute fetched code, making it a reproducibility concern rather than a security injection. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' verdict was caused by an HTTP 400 API error during PKGBUILD review, not by any security finding. The openrouter report (advisory only) also found the package safe with the same reasoning about unpinned docs being a reproducibility issue, not malice.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures, not security analysis. The qwen model failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to an HTTP 400 error, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found no malicious code. The openrouter/free report (advisory, not counted) also completed successfully and agreed with deepseek's assessment.
coverage_issues: qwen model: PKGBUILD full review failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError
openrouter model: .SRCINFO review failed with empty LLM response
learnings: Tool errors (HTTP failures, empty responses) should be clearly distinguished from security findings - an API failure is not evidence of malicious code

Models should be trained to recognize that fetching supplementary content (docs/examples) from a project's own repository at build time, even from an unpinned ref, is a reproducibility concern rather than a security injection when no fetched code is executed
The audit tool should implement retry logic for transient API failures to avoid inconclusive verdicts caused by infrastructure issues rather than security concerns
